R0237.title: Ad Click Injection
R0237.definition: Attackers inject fake clicks before installation or conversion to steal attribution revenue.
R0237.description:
Ad click injection forges click events shortly before an install, open, or conversion to steal attribution from organic traffic or other channels. Attackers often use malicious SDKs, background services, or device permissions to fabricate clicks.

The risk distorts campaign measurement and makes advertisers pay for hijacked conversions. Anti-fraud analysis should examine click-to-conversion time, device behavior, SDK source, and channel distribution.
R0237.influence: Click injection steals real conversion attribution, wastes ad budget, and distorts channel evaluation and bidding strategy.

observables: Click-to-conversion time windows are abnormally short or inconsistent with normal install behavior
The same device or SDK source generates attribution clicks across multiple channels
Channel attribution distribution shows anomalous concentration or sudden shifts
Fake click events are bulk-injected before installs or conversions
Advertisers pay for hijacked conversions with no valid user value
